scopeDecisions.decision: The declared SDKs compared end to end are the Admin SDK for Node (firebase-admin 14.3.0) and the Web SDK (firebase 12.18.0) as far as it runs in Node. Browser and mobile SDKs are out of scope for this parent; browser paths are taken up with FS-LISTEN-SDK and the other browser-bound parents.

reCAPTCHA is observed as the recaptchaConfig read, write and validation, and the results of requests while no provider enforces (OFF and AUDIT). ENFORCE and the verification of reCAPTCHA tokens are out of scope: a genuine token cannot be produced outside a browser.

The configuration of a new project matches production exactly under the strict profile. Under the emulator profile fireemu keeps the fields the official emulator reports (signIn.allowDuplicateEmails false, emailPrivacyConfig.enableImprovedEmailPrivacy false, blockingFunctions {}) and, like both of them, reports no passwordPolicyConfig and no client.permissions switches.

Sign-up quota (moved here by AUTH-ACCOUNT A7, AUTH-CREDENTIAL C8 and AUTH-ACTION E7) is observed as the quota.signUpQuotaConfig read, write and validation. Enforcement (production's per-IP limit of about 100 sign-ups per hour and a configured quota) is a known production refusal fireemu does not implement: observing it would stop the other lanes that share the sandbox and its egress address. Any HTTP 429 or quota refusal in this corpus is INDETERMINATE.

SDK programs run against fireemu under the strict profile with auth.idTokenSigning unsigned-emulator, the configuration the Admin SDK needs for verifyIdToken while FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST is set. Where the SDK's own emulator mode behaves unlike production (it verifies no signature, and it checks revocation and disabled users even when checkRevoked is false), the difference belongs to the SDK and is recorded as a documented divergence, not a fireemu mismatch. Because strict refuses unsigned custom tokens (AUTH-CREDENTIAL follow-up decision), the createCustomToken-to-sign-in program runs against the emulator profile.

Production createCustomToken needs IAM signBlob. The owner user may hold a custom role with iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob only on firebase-adminsdk-fbsvc@fireemu-oracle-idp, bound with a time condition for the recording only and removed afterwards; every change goes into the sandbox change log and the owner ledger.

If production refuses an AUDIT recaptchaConfig because the reCAPTCHA Enterprise API is disabled, the API may be enabled on the Identity Platform sandbox. ENFORCE is never set; AUDIT is restored to its prior state at the end of the program.

notification (email and SMS templates, callbackUri, defaultLocale) is a configuration field: under strict its initial value is production's, and a PATCH is stored and read back. Nothing is mailed or rendered with it (AUTH-ACTION E1).

Project MFA configuration (mfa, and the Admin SDK multiFactorConfig beyond reading it) belongs to AUTH-MFA and is left out of this parent's comparison projection, because that lane changes it on the shared sandbox.

Multi-tenancy (multiTenant), tenant configuration and the tenant inheritance of project settings (moved here by AUTH-ACCOUNT A3), and blocking functions belong to AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING and are left out of this parent's comparison projection.

The effects of duplicate emails, email privacy, the password policy and client permissions on the account routes AUTH-ACCOUNT recorded are closed there (AUTH-ACCOUNT A3) and are not recorded again. This parent records the configuration itself, the policy projections to clients and SDKs, and the configuration-dependent results AUTH-ACCOUNT did not observe.

Key material in the configuration (signIn.hashConfig.signerKey and saltSeparator, client.apiKey) is recorded as placeholders, and the harness never writes a read-only path whose change could alter it (signIn.hashConfig, client.apiKey). Read-only paths are exercised through name, subtype and defaultHostingSite only.

An omitted or empty updateMask is not observed on the shared sandbox, and the harness refuses to send one: production's reading of either is undocumented, and if it replaced every settable member the harness could not write back the members other lanes own (mfa, multiTenant, blockingFunctions). fireemu keeps its present reading (an empty mask changes nothing; an omitted mask is inferred from the members present) until either is observed on a project no other lane uses. Recorded as an unobserved edge.

The sign-in providers (email/password, passwordRequired, anonymous, phone and test numbers) start enabled in both profiles, although a new production project enables none: a real project always enables what it uses, and a strict default of none would stop every first sign-up. The difference from production's initial configuration is known and recorded here; the startup key auth.signIn carries a production project's providers over.

The client v2/recaptchaConfig answered 500 while a provider was AUDIT although the PATCH was accepted, so recaptchaenterprise.googleapis.com was enabled on the Identity Platform sandbox to observe the AUDIT shape and the requests without a token; the API stays enabled and the change is in the sandbox change log (widens K7). Owner ledger 2026-09-25, AUTH-CONFIG-SDK K15.

A malformed JSON body (config/invalid#body-malformed) is a known difference in its message only: production appends its protobuf JSON parser's diagnostic ('Unexpected end of string. Expected an object key or }.' and a caret line), fireemu answers the same 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT with 'Invalid JSON payload received.'. Whether to reproduce common diagnostics is tracked separately (protobuf-json-parser-diagnostics). Owner ledger 2026-09-25.

While a provider is AUDIT, production's client v2/recaptchaConfig answered 500 INTERNAL on the sandbox (recaptcha#client-audit-web, -ios, -android, -phone and #client-cleared), because no reCAPTCHA Enterprise key can be provisioned there even with the API enabled (K15). This is a difference the sandbox cannot observe; fireemu keeps answering the configured enforcement states with 200 and no key, and the configuration's read and write match production. Owner ledger 2026-09-25.

The final-artifact regression re-runs the AUTH-ACCOUNT, AUTH-CREDENTIAL and AUTH-ACTION corpora and inherits their one documented divergence: AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A12, the gson parser message text for malformed customAttributes JSON (as AUTH-ACTION E9 inherits it).

conditions.note: The Admin GET config at the sandbox baseline, member for member (which unset members are absent, false switches omitted, the name with the project number, subtype, read-only members), and the client configuration reads at the same state: v1/projects, v2/passwordPolicy with no policy set, v2/recaptchaConfig with none set and without clientType, v1/recaptchaParams by shape.

The PATCH answer and the read-back for a leaf mask, a parent mask, a masked path absent from the body (reset), a body member outside the mask (ignored), an unknown path, a duplicate path, and a read-only path (name, subtype, defaultHostingSite, written back with its current value). An omitted or empty mask is K13.

Refusals (status, code and message) of invalid values outside the password policy: test phone numbers and codes, authorized domains, mobileLinksConfig, smsRegionConfig, wrong JSON types, unknown members, and a body that is not an object; and that a refused PATCH changes nothing.

documentedDivergences.reason: production's protobuf JSON parser appends its diagnostic to 'Invalid JSON payload received.'; the 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT refusal matches.

conditions.note: passwordPolicyConfig writes: accepted shapes and their read-back (schemaVersion, lastUpdateTime, forceUpgradeOnSignin omitted when false, the cleared state), and refusals of lengths out of range, a maximum below the minimum, fractional lengths, zero or two versions, an unspecified state, and ENFORCE without a version.

An account whose password does not meet a policy set after it was created: sign-in under ENFORCE with forceUpgradeOnSignin (refused or not) and without it (userNotifications), under OFF, a compliant password change, a reset through an Admin-generated code, and the Admin update route under the default policy.

Results while email/password, anonymous or phone sign-in is disabled: client sign-up and sign-in, password reset, phone code requests and sign-in on test numbers, and the Admin routes, which the switches do not restrict.
